newsitem.title: USA: IRS enforcement program a wake up call to market.
newsitem.headline: IRS enforcement program a wake up call to market.

text.p: Municipal bond industry representatives said on Monday that last week's Internal Revenue Service update on the status of IRS' bond audit program is a wake up call for market players.

"It alerts people to the fact that the IRS enforcement program is up and running," Amy Dunbar, director of governmental affairs for the National Association of Bond Lawyers, said concerning statements by two IRS officials at the group's Washington seminar here on May 9.
"People have started to take into account the fact that there is a Securities and Exchange Commission enforcement program during the course of the past couple of years," Dunbar said.

"Charles Anderson was living proof that the IRS program is up and running as well," Dunbar said, referring to a presentation by Anderson, who oversees all muni bond audits in IRS' 14-state Southeast region.

Anderson said his offce has notified 30 muni issuers in the past five months that their bonds, issued on a tax-exempt basis, are probably taxable. The Southeast region will send up to 50 more notices by November, he said.
"It's quite astounding the number of cases we have going," Anderson said.
Gerald Sack, a top official in IRS' exempt organizations division here, added that the Service has entered into eight "closing agreements" with bond issuers since early 1996.

Catherine Spain, director of the Government Finance Officers Association's Washington office said issuers, particularly issuers of conduit bonds, may be feeling the weight of a lot of new tax and securities law changes from Washington.

"There have been a lot of changes that do affect a lot of conduit financings," said Spain, noting that GFOA's members typically do not handle the type of small issue financing that may be the focus of many of the pending closing agreements.
"In years past, a lot of governments just approved these financings with a feeling that we're not on the hook for any of this. But things can go awry in some of these transactions," Spain said.

Spain said she is surprised by the sheer number of pending closing agreements. "What's incredible is that all that stuff is going out," she said, referring to IRS's notices to localities. "I haven't heard a word from issuers. (It's) incredible."
"Are these all small issue IDBs or what the heck are these? Are these cases where the law was so complex that people didn't understand it?" Spain asked.
John Murphy, executive director of the Association of Local Housing Finance Agencies, also said he wants more inforamtion.

"It would be instructive to have them identify whether there are patterns here. "What's causing these seeming violations? Are they highly technical and insequential or are they serious breeches," Murphy said.
